find: the Suspension Clause does not apply, and because she was apprehended immediately after unlawful entry at the threshold of the border, statutory procedure satisfies due process
replace: the Suspension Clause does not require review of that claim. If the court treats her as still at the threshold of initial entry, as the proximity to the border and short elapsed time suggest, due process requires only the admission procedures Congress provided
reason: Thuraissigiam addressed what relief the Suspension Clause protects. Its due process holding rested on the threshold-of-entry facts and did not adopt a fixed distance or time limit.
